liquid.survey: ECB Distributional Wealth Accounts (HFCS distributions aligned to the national financial accounts)

note: The World Inequality Database (WID.world, bulk download of 15 October 2026, read again in that of 30 October 2026), Ireland, 2024: average net personal wealth (ahweal992j) and average post-tax national income (adiinc992j) per adult over 20, resources split equally within couples, in EUR of that year, for the bottom 20, 40, 60, 90 and 99 percent and the top 1 percent; each family's band is read from them. Read 2026-10-30. Savings (the owner's ruling of 2026-10-30: only what a family holds as deposits and cash): The ECB's Distributional Wealth Accounts (dataset DWA, read through the ECB Data Portal API on 2026-10-30, latest quarter 2026-Q1) split the household sector's balance sheet of IE by net-wealth quintile and by the top five net-wealth deciles, built from the Household Finance and Consumption Survey and scaled to the national financial and non-financial accounts. Per household, in euro (the API gives thousands; multiplied by 1000 here): deposits (instrument F2M), net wealth (NWA), total assets and total liabilities (F_NNA). No top 1 percent and no separate bottom deciles 1 to 5 are published; B50 is the bottom half. Deposits include currency only as far as the national accounts' F2M instrument does (deposits; currency F21 is not separated). depositsShareOfNetWealth is my division of the two published means; it is above 1 or negative wherever the band's net wealth is small or negative (Quintile 1). Units are households, while WID's bands are adults with equal split; the mapping in "band" is by percentile position only. Read again 2026-11-03 from the bulk download of 30 October 2026 (its country files dated 30 October 2026): every row quoted here, its year and its currency label stood as before, and no later year was given. Until 2026-11-03 this note and its sources wrote the variable codes with their age and population parts swapped (ahwealj992 for ahweal992j and adiincj992 for adiinc992j), codes no file of the database holds (its README: type, concept, age group, population, as in sptinc992j), and called adiinc992j post-tax disposable income, which its metadata names post-tax national income ([Post-tax national income]=[Post-tax disposable income]+[Public spending]). Its other sources were fetched again on 2026-11-03 and said the same. The national accounts (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-03: each band's income scaled by households' disposable income over national income), read 2026-11-03 from Eurostat's non-financial transactions (nasa_10_nf_tr), 2024: the net disposable income (B.6n) of households (S.14), 169,058, and net national income (B.5n) 289,431, in millions of the national currency, a ratio of about 0.584 (`cash`). Until 2026-11-03 each band's income was the database's post-tax national income as it stood, public spending included.
